//Cors: Blank on purpose; supplied per deployment as Cors__AllowedOrigins__0 and so on. Needs the platform's own origin AND a wildcard for restaurant websites - https://*.example.com - or the guest ordering and review screens on a restaurant's own host are answered without an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and the browser discards the reply. Nothing fails on this side when that happens, so it presents as pages that look broken for no reason.
//ForwardedHeaders: Which proxies may say who the visitor really is. Behind the Next /api proxy (API_PROXY_TARGET) every request arrives from that server, so without this the rate limits treat the whole platform as one visitor. Name the proxy's address in KnownProxies, or its range in KnownNetworks (CIDR, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8). TrustAllProxies is for a proxy with no fixed address and is safe ONLY if this API cannot be reached except through it - otherwise anybody can forge the header and walk past every limit.
//Bootstrap: Blank on purpose. The bootstrap only runs once both Email and Password are set, so this file starting empty means a deployment that has not been told who the first administrator is creates nobody rather than creating a default one. Development supplies them in appsettings.Development.json; production supplies Bootstrap__SuperAdmin__Email and Bootstrap__SuperAdmin__Password as environment variables.
